title: The genus is invariant under extension
statement:
Let $C$ be a proper smooth connected curve over
$k$ and let $k\subseteq k'$ be algebraically closed. Then

$$
g(C_{k'})=g(C),
$$

compatibly with the Jacobian of
[thm-sc-jacobian-representability] (i.e. $J_{C_{k'}}\cong(J_C)_{k'}$, and the identifications of
[def-sc-jacobian] are compatible with base change).

proof.text: A connected scheme over a separably closed field is geometrically connected. Smoothness then gives geometric irreducibility and geometric reducedness, hence geometric integrality, using the Regular library. Base change preserves these geometric properties; baseChange_curve supplies the connected-curve structure. Smooth irreducible dimension-one schemes have smooth relative dimension one.
Rewrite both genera as arithmetic genera using genus_eq_arithmeticGenus and apply arithmeticGenus_pullback, the structure-sheaf specialization of flat coherent base change.

Apply exists_jacobian separately over k and K. Its proper, smooth and geometrically integral representing group scheme is an abelian variety. Its dimension equals the arithmetic genus by smooth relative dimension and therefore the genus. Repackage its representation as IsJacobian.
Apply the isolated Jacobian compatibility square to the two chosen representations.
